title: Dimension-dependent real junta approximation
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and $\varepsilon>0$. There exist $J\subseteq[n]$ and $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ depending only on $J$, with $|J|\le4nI(f)/\varepsilon$ and $\mathbb E(f-g)^2\le\varepsilon$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n
replaced:
(Friedgut, 1998.) Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ and let $\varepsilon > 0$.
Then there are a coordinate set $J$ and a function $g$ such that
$\abs{J} \le 4n\,I[f]/\varepsilon$, the function $g$ is a $J$-junta, and
$\E\big[(f - g)^2\big] \le \varepsilon$.
